modalities.name: CT
modalities.description: Computed tomography resolves internal anatomy through cross-sectional X-ray images. Here, the 2D collection represents individual slices.

media.author: 3D Slicer / Brigham and Women’s Hospital
media.caption: An axial CT slice from the 3D Slicer sample data.
media.alt: An axial CT slice from the 3D Slicer sample data.

modalities.name: Histopathology
modalities.description: Microscopy of prepared tissue reveals cellular morphology and tissue architecture. The tokenizer represents these fine textures alongside larger-scale anatomy.

modalities.name: MRI
modalities.description: Magnetic resonance imaging provides rich soft-tissue contrast. Individual slices capture anatomical structures with a range of acquisition sequences and contrasts.

media.author: 3D Slicer / Brigham and Women’s Hospital
media.caption: An axial MRI slice from the 3D Slicer sample data.
media.alt: An axial MRI slice from the 3D Slicer sample data.

modalities.name: Fundus
modalities.description: Fundus photography records the retinal surface, including the optic disc, macula, and blood vessels, in a single color image.

media.author: Mikael Häggström
media.caption: Fundus photograph of a normal left eye.
media.alt: Fundus photograph of a normal left eye.

modalities.name: Endoscopy
modalities.description: A camera inside the body records the surface of organs and cavities. These images capture mucosal texture, folds, and local lesions.

modalities.name: X-ray
modalities.description: Projection radiography compresses three-dimensional anatomy into a two-dimensional image. Bones and chest structures appear through differences in X-ray attenuation.

modalities.name: Dermoscopy
modalities.description: Magnified skin imaging reveals pigment patterns and surface structures that are difficult to see with the unaided eye.

media.author: Raimundo Pastor
media.caption: Dermoscopic photograph of an intradermal melanocytic nevus.
media.alt: Dermoscopic photograph of an intradermal melanocytic nevus.

modalities.name: Ultrasound
modalities.description: Reflected sound waves reveal soft-tissue boundaries and internal organ structure. Characteristic speckle and acoustic shadows distinguish this modality.

media.author: Mikael Häggström
media.caption: Ultrasound image of a normal liver.
media.alt: Ultrasound image of a normal liver.

modalities.name: OCT
modalities.description: Optical coherence tomography uses light to resolve fine cross-sectional tissue layers, including the layered structure of the retina.

media.author: Wies6014
media.caption: OCT cross-sections of a healthy optic disc.
media.alt: OCT cross-sections of a healthy optic disc.

modalities.name: CT
modalities.description: A CT volume preserves anatomy across a stack of X-ray slices. Native 3D tokenization captures spatial relationships between slices, beyond an isolated cross-section.

media.author: 3D Slicer / Brigham and Women’s Hospital
media.caption: CT volume; three orthogonal slices form the cube.
media.alt: An axial CT slice from the 3D Slicer sample data.

modalities.name: MRI
modalities.description: An MRI volume preserves soft-tissue anatomy across three spatial dimensions. Native 3D tokens represent the volume as one input while retaining relationships between neighboring slices.

media.author: 3D Slicer / Brigham and Women’s Hospital
media.caption: MRI volume; three orthogonal slices form the cube.
media.alt: An axial MRI slice from the 3D Slicer sample data.
